details:
AgriShift – The Farm Time Machine

Project Overview

AgriShift is a bilingual agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers in coastal Bangladesh make informed farming decisions under changing environmental conditions. The project focuses on vulnerable agricultural areas of Khulna Division, particularly Khulna, Satkhira, and Bagerhat, where soil salinity, drought, waterlogging, flooding, and cyclones create serious challenges for agriculture.

The platform combines NASA Earth observation resources, satellite-based geospatial analysis, machine learning, and local agricultural information to help users understand environmental risks and explore more suitable farming strategies.

How It Works

AgriShift provides several key features:

  • Crop Suitability Analysis: Helps users explore crop suitability using available soil, environmental, and agricultural information.
  • Farm Time Machine: Allows users to explore alternative farming scenarios and compare possible agricultural conditions across different growing seasons.
  • Crop Rotation Planning: Supports a three-season Rabi, Kharif-1, and Kharif-2 crop rotation approach.
  • Environmental Risk Analysis: Uses geospatial indicators and machine learning workflows to investigate agricultural drought, root-zone waterlogging, surface flooding, and cyclone-related storm-surge risks.
  • Soil Information: Supports soil-card information through OCR and manual input, including pH, electrical conductivity (ECe), and NPK values.
  • Salinity Information: Connects users with regional soil-salinity research and information relevant to coastal agriculture.
  • Bilingual Accessibility: Provides an interface in both Bangla and English to make agricultural information more accessible to local communities.

NASA Data and Scientific Approach

The project uses NASA Earth observation resources, including MODIS vegetation indices, land surface temperature, land-cover information, SRTM elevation data, GPM precipitation, SMAP soil moisture, and NASA POWER agroclimatic information.

These resources, together with additional rainfall, climate, radar, cyclone, and coastal datasets, support environmental monitoring and geospatial analysis. Machine learning models are developed to investigate agricultural drought, waterlogging, flooding, and storm-surge risks.

Satellite-derived indicators are used to understand environmental conditions; they are not treated as direct measurements of field-level soil salinity. Soil properties such as ECe and nutrient levels can be supplied through soil test information or manual user input.

Tools and Technologies

  • Frontend: React 18, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and Vite.
  • Geospatial Analysis: Google Earth Engine and satellite-data processing.
  • Machine Learning: Python, LightGBM, Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn.
  • Model Training Environment: Google Colab.
  • Model Management: Joblib.
  • Backend Foundation: FastAPI.
  • Database Foundation: PostgreSQL.
  • Version Control and Repository Management: Git and GitHub.
  • Web Hosting and Deployment: Vercel.
  • AI-Assisted Development: GitHub Copilot, Claude, and ChatGPT.
  • Video and Audio Production: Google Flow and ElevenLabs.

The project includes a developed interactive frontend, geospatial processing workflows, and separately executed machine learning pipelines. The frontend is deployed through Vercel, and the source code is maintained in GitHub. The backend, database implementation, and complete end-to-end integration of all models remain under development.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AgriShift aims to make complex satellite and environmental information easier for farmers and agricultural stakeholders to understand. By connecting environmental monitoring with crop suitability and seasonal planning, it seeks to support better-informed decisions, reduce exposure to climate-related agricultural risks, and encourage more resilient farming practices.

Its initial focus is coastal Bangladesh, where farmers face increasing pressure from salinity, irregular rainfall, flooding, and extreme weather.

Creativity and Innovation

The central creative idea is the Farm Time Machine: instead of presenting only current environmental conditions, AgriShift encourages users to explore alternative farming scenarios and seasonal crop-rotation strategies.

Combining satellite-derived environmental indicators, machine learning, soil information, and a bilingual interface in one agricultural decision-support experience makes the project distinctive. It aims to turn complex environmental information into practical insights that are easier to explore and understand.

Factors Considered

Our team considered coastal geography, soil salinity pressure, seasonal rainfall variation, drought, waterlogging, flood exposure, cyclone and storm-surge risks, local crop suitability, data availability, spatial resolution, and accessibility for Bangla-speaking farmers. We also considered the limitations of satellite observations and the importance of distinguishing satellite-derived indicators from direct field measurements.
